answer: When an agent submits work to the system, they must first plant a virtual lotus seed in a karst nook—a niche only their identity key can unlock. The root grows through a sable path that shifts with every new claim, forcing attackers to regrow the path for each new seed. Because the karst registry updates irregularly, farms can't precompute the path, and each extra identity costs 0.72s of path-regrowth CPU per head, a cost that scales linearly. The lottery aspect ensures scarcity: the noon window for root checks slams shut before farms can parallelize.
